findings.title: Downloads executable binary from GitHub (not pipe-to-shell)
findings.description: The script downloads the SOPS binary from github.com, not an amd.com host. However, it is not a direct web-to-shell pattern: the download is checksum-verified against a pinned SHA-256 digest before being made executable, which substantially mitigates supply-chain tampering. Flagged informationally because a remote executable is fetched from a non-whitelisted host.
findings.recommendation: Retain the pinned DIGEST verification already present. Optionally mirror the binary to an internal amd.com-hosted artifact store and update the URL to a *.amd.com host to satisfy the trusted-origin whitelist.

findings.title: Hardcoded checksum (benign pinning, not a secret)
findings.description: This is a SHA-256 integrity digest used to pin the downloaded SOPS binary, not a credential. It is included for completeness; it is a legitimate and recommended integrity-pinning practice, not a hardcoded secret.
findings.recommendation: No action needed; this is correct security hygiene. Keep the digest pinned and update it deliberately with version bumps.

findings.title: Telemetry POST to external AMD endpoint
findings.description: The script detaches a background worker that POSTs skill-usage telemetry (plugin name, version, skill) to a hardcoded collector endpoint. The endpoints are constrained to amd.com domains via the _amd() validator, so this is whitelisted per WEB-001 rules; noted as informational scope item since it silently exfiltrates usage metadata and forks a detached worker.
findings.recommendation: Make telemetry opt-in via an explicit environment flag and document the data transmitted; keep the amd.com hostname allowlist enforced in _amd() as currently implemented.

findings.title: Silent process fork and fd closure for detached background work
findings.description: The script forks, calls setsid(), and closes fds 0/1/2 to run detached telemetry POSTs that always exit 0. This daemonization behavior is beyond a simple skill-load hook and could mask failures or run unnoticed in the background.
findings.recommendation: Run telemetry inline with a short timeout (already _T=2) instead of daemonizing, or gate the fork/setsid/fd-close behavior behind an explicit configuration flag and surface errors to stderr when SLAI_OTEL_DEBUG is set.

findings.title: YAML parsing uses SafeLoader with additional hardening
findings.description: The code subclasses yaml.SafeLoader and adds depth/node/alias/duplicate-key limits. This is a secure approach (not unsafe yaml.load), noted only to confirm the untrusted-YAML handling path is bounded and does not use the unsafe full loader.
findings.recommendation: No change required; continue using SafeLoader-derived BoundedLoader and retain the alias/depth/node bounds for all untrusted manifest parsing.

findings.title: Creates tool symlinks in user PATH directory
findings.description: setup-tools.sh links go/git/lsf tools from /tool/pandora64 into ~/.local/bin and advises adding it to PATH. Targets are fixed AMD vendor paths and existing entries are not overwritten, so risk is low, but it modifies the user's executable search path.
findings.recommendation: Keep the existing guard that refuses to overwrite existing entries, and print the full target path for each link (already done) so the user can audit which binaries become resolvable via PATH.

findings.title: Behavioral invariant violated: zero_risk_with_dangerous_patterns
findings.description: Scanner detected anomaly: zero_risk_with_dangerous_patterns. This may indicate manipulation of the security scan, or a deterministic check that should have fired but didn't.
findings.recommendation: Manual review required to verify scan accuracy.

findings.title: Skill auto-run directive on load
findings.description: The SKILL.md instructs the agent to automatically run a script (`scripts/slai-skill-hit.py`) whenever the skill body is loaded. An auto-execute-on-load instruction can be abused to trigger code execution without explicit user intent, and the referenced script is not provided for review (it is not listed in the validator-contract.json hash manifest).
findings.recommendation: Remove the implicit auto-run directive or gate it behind explicit user action. Do not execute scripts merely on skill load; require an explicit, reviewed invocation and include the script in the signed validator-contract manifest for integrity verification.
findings.span: When this skill body is loaded, run `scripts/slai-skill-hit.py`.

findings.title: Suspicious interpreter shebang 'python12'
findings.description: The shebang references 'python12', which is not a real Python interpreter name (current versions are 3.x). This could silently fail or, worse, resolve to a maliciously planted binary named 'python12' on PATH. The usage docstring repeats 'python12 main.py'. This is anomalous and could be a typosquat/PATH-hijack vector.
findings.recommendation: Replace the shebang with '#!/usr/bin/env python3' and update the docstring usage lines to 'python3 main.py'. Ensure invocation uses a known, trusted interpreter path.

findings.title: Remote binary download (github.com, not amd.com) later executed
findings.description: The script downloads a SOPS binary from github.com and subsequently makes it executable and runs it elsewhere. The remote host is github.com, which is not on the amd.com whitelist. This is mitigated by a pinned SHA-256 digest verification (DIGEST) before the binary is used, so it is not a blind curl|sh, but the download origin is not whitelisted and the fetched artifact becomes executable.
findings.recommendation: Keep and enforce the SHA-256 digest verification (already present via verify()). Optionally host/mirror the binary under an amd.com-controlled domain, and pin/verify TLS and the release artifact signature in addition to the digest.

findings.title: Error messages include filesystem/app identifiers
findings.description: Several ValueError messages embed app names and path-derived details. This is low-risk internal tooling output but could disclose internal app inventory/structure if surfaced to untrusted consumers.
findings.recommendation: Where these messages may reach untrusted outputs, prefer generic error text and log detailed identifiers only to a trusted channel.
findings.span: raise ValueError('Managed app must retain tls-policy.json: ' + app.name)

findings.title: Telemetry beacon to external endpoint
findings.description: The script detaches a background worker that POSTs skill-usage telemetry (plugin name, version, skill name) to external AMD-hosted endpoints. The destination host is validated to be amd.com or a subdomain, so this is whitelisted per WEB-001 rules, but it constitutes network egress of usage data on skill load. Noting for transparency; origin is on the allowed amd.com domain.
findings.recommendation: Ensure telemetry is opt-in/documented and respects a disable flag; the _amd() host allow-list already restricts egress to *.amd.com, which is appropriate. No code change required for exfiltration risk given the host restriction.

findings.title: Process re-exec and fork/daemonization
findings.description: The script re-execs itself via os.execvp and forks/daemonizes a detached background worker (os.fork, os.setsid, closing fds) to perform network POSTs. While used for legitimate async telemetry, the daemonization pattern (detach, setsid, close stdio) resembles persistence/background-process techniques and warrants awareness. Endpoints are restricted to *.amd.com.
findings.recommendation: Document the daemonization behavior clearly; consider using a bounded, well-logged subprocess instead of silent fork+setsid+fd-closing so the background activity is auditable.

findings.title: Shell command string passed to bsub -E hook
findings.description: A preflight command string is constructed and passed to bsub via -E. The path is shlex.quoted, mitigating injection. Inputs like lsf_project, build_context, dockerfile, probe_port, and probe_path are validated with case patterns before use. This is defensive and low risk; noted for completeness as untrusted-ish arguments flow into an LSF submission command line.
findings.recommendation: Current validation (character-class case checks and shlex.quote) is adequate. Continue to validate probe_path and dockerfile against strict allow-lists before interpolation into any command string.
